Write a Wave as an AudioMoth triggered (T.WAV) file

Source: R/audiomothTWav.R
audiomothCompress.Rd

Writes a mono 16-bit Wave object in the AudioMoth triggered file format, leaving out the periods that an amplitude threshold would not have triggered a recording on. The wave is divided into segments of segment bytes, and a segment whose peak amplitude is below threshold is omitted and replaced by an encoded block recording its length. Omitted audio is not recoverable: expanding the file gives silence in its place, as it would for a recording the device had made with that threshold.

Usage

audiomothCompress(
  wave,
  file,
  threshold,
  segment = .AM_SEGMENT_SIZE,
  comment = "",
  artist = "",
  guano = NULL,
  overwrite = FALSE
)

Arguments

wave

A mono 16-bit Wave object

file

Path to write the T.WAV file to

threshold

Peak amplitude, as a 16-bit sample value, at or above which a segment is kept. This is the amplitude threshold of an AudioMoth device.

segment

Length of a segment in bytes. Must be a multiple of 512 and longer than the 488-byte header. The default of 32768 is what current AudioMoth firmware uses.

comment

Comment string to store in the header, of the kind readMetadata() reads back as its audiomoth source. The threshold is recorded after it, as an AudioMoth device records it, which is how readAudio() knows to expand the file.

artist

Artist string to store in the header

guano

GUANO metadata to store in the file, as a guano object from guano() or guanoCreate(), or NULL for none

overwrite

If TRUE an existing file is replaced

Value

The path to the written file (invisibly)

Details

The threshold is recorded in the comment the file carries, in the wording an AudioMoth device uses, so that the file says what was done to it. There is nothing else in a wave file to tell a triggered recording from any other, and it is what readAudio() reads to know that the file needs expanding.

The first and last segments are never omitted, as the first holds the file header and the last may be shorter than a whole segment. Where these fall below the threshold they are written as silence, which is what AudioMoth firmware does.

References

Open Acoustic Devices (2021) AudioMoth Triggered T.WAV File Format. https://github.com/OpenAcousticDevices/Application-Notes

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
w <- readAudio(system.file("extdata/AUDIOMOTH.WAV", package="sonicscrewdriver"))
audiomothCompress(w, "20201103_112430T.WAV", threshold=1000)
} # }
